Houston by the numbers

Houston knows it has a traffic problem.

49%name bad roads one of Houston's top three problems.
37%name traffic congestion one of the top three.
52%say bad streets seriously hurt their neighborhood.

University of Houston Hobby School survey of 1,400 Houston voters, April 2025.

Houston makes it harder

Trains cut the city in pieces

Freight lines run straight through Houston neighborhoods. Texas leads the nation in reports of trains blocking crossings, and in 2025 the City of Houston launched its own Train Watch tool to track them.

Rain turns roads into rivers

One heavy storm can flood an underpass fast. On a regular map, a road that's just slow and a road that's underwater look exactly the same.

It's a city built on freeways

Houston is spread out, so almost every trip uses a freeway. When one backs up, the side streets fill too, and guessing wrong about why can cost you the whole evening.

Sources University of Houston Hobby School of Public Affairs, City of Houston 2025 survey (April 2025) Houston TranStar, Historical Freeway Travel Times, 2025 "Texas leads the nation in blocked railroad crossings, according to federal data," KHOU City of Houston launches Train Watch, ABC13 (Aug 2025)
